items.title: Euro zone economy slows to 0.4% growth in Q3 as crisis-hit France contracts
items.summary: The euro zone showed surprising resilience, but weak productivity, industrial competitiveness challenges and demographic pressures remain, analysts said.
items.body: Economic expansion in the euro zone slowed to 0.4% in the third quarter, statistics agency Eurostat said on Friday. The 21-nation euro area rebounded to 0.6% growth in the second quarter, following stagnation in the first three months of the year. The flash third quarter reading was nonetheless higher than the 0.2% growth that was forecast in a Reuters poll of economists. However, France's economy unexpectedly contracted by 0.1% over the July to September period. The country is grappling with soaring borrowing costs as investors balk at a political struggle to reduce its high budget deficit and mounting national debt. October has also brought growing nationwide unrest over the cost of living and other issues, which has at times escalated into violent and costly rioting . Germany, the euro zone's largest economy, grew by just 0.2% in the third quarter.

items.title: Crypto giant Binance attempting to recover $6.3bn stolen in hack linked to North Korea
items.summary: The cyber-attack, which the company describes as complex, is believed to be the largest ever of its kind.
items.body: Binance, the world's largest cryptocurrency exchange, says it has frozen around half of the funds stolen in a "complex" hack, after $6.3bn (£4.7bn) was accessed in what is believed to be a record heist. The firm said $3bn of its stolen digital assets had been secured - but many were still in the hands of unidentified hackers. It initially thought an engineer's laptop had been compromised, allowing unauthorised withdrawals, but later said the attack was wider. Several analytics firms have linked the hack, which eclipses a $1.5bn (£1.12bn) heist on the Bybit exchange in 2025, to a North Korean hacking unit. The US Secret Service said it was "working around the clock" "to identify, freeze, trace, and recover" stolen funds.

items.body: Germany's annual inflation rate eased to 2.8% in October from 3.3% in September, with economists pointing to the government's fuel tax cut as the main reason. Preliminary figures from the Federal Statistical Office showed energy prices rose 12.2% compared with a year earlier, down from 14.9% in September. Services inflation slowed to 2.5%, while food inflation remained at 0.4%. "The decisive factor was the fuel tax cut," said Silke Tober of the Macroeconomic Policy Institute. The reduction took effect in October and runs through December, although rising crude oil prices partly offset the savings at the pump. ING bank economist Carsten Brzeski said higher energy costs had yet to feed through into broader price increases. Unlike during the 2022 energy crisis, consumers were unwilling or unable to absorb substantially higher prices, he said.

items.title: Philip R. Lane: AI adoption in Europe
items.body: My aim today is to describe how AI is reshaping the euro area economy. [ 2 ] In addition, European firms are part of the global AI supply chain, while European investors are contributing to the funding of the global buildout of AI infrastructure through equity and debt markets and the banking system. items.title: Chinese telecoms giants in Washington’s crosshairs as FCC weighs fresh curbs
items.summary: The US Federal Communications Commission (FCC) is proposing a ban on Chinese telecommunications companies obtaining American telephone numbers, citing national security concerns and the need to protect domestic networks. The proposed rules could prevent China Mobile, China…
items.body: The US Federal Communications Commission (FCC) is proposing a ban on Chinese telecommunications companies obtaining American telephone numbers, citing national security concerns and the need to protect domestic networks. The proposed rules could prevent China Mobile, China Telecom and China Unicom and other service providers from obtaining numbers through internet-based voice services, the commission said on Thursday. The regulator is scheduled to vote on the proposal at its November 19 meeting. The measures, it said, were intended to protect against illegal robocalls and other malicious activity while addressing national security risks linked with foreign-controlled communications networks.

items.title: Tankers defy sharp escalation of Iranian attacks to keep crude oil flowing through Strait of Hormuz
items.summary: Soaring freight rates are giving tankers a big financial incentive to run the gauntlet through the Strait of Hormuz.
items.body: Within 24 hours of the U.S. and Israel going to war with Iran, Tehran responded with a wave of attacks on commercial ships in the Strait of Hormuz to cut off one of the world's main sources of crude oil. Iran's campaign was initially successful, with crude exports plunging nearly 90% to 1.8 million barrels a day in March compared with 16 million bpd in February, according to data provided by Kpler. But crude flows have rebounded over the past eight months as the U.S. military provides protection to tankers transiting Hormuz. Tehran has responded by escalating its attacks in recent weeks . More commercial ships have come under attack in October than at any other point in the war. Yet in contrast to March when exports cratered, tankers have continued to ferry substantial volumes of crude oil through Hormuz in a sign that the shipping industry has adapted to wartime in the Persian Gulf.

items.title: US tech stocks see sharp falls as AI spending nears $1tn
items.summary: Shares in Intel continue to fall while the tech-heavy Nasdaq opens at its lowest level in more than two months.
items.body: Tech stocks tumbled for the second day in a row as concerns rise over the hundreds of billions of dollars firms are investing in artificial intelligence (AI). Shares in Intel plummeted by 28% on Friday, while Google owner Alphabet saw its stock price continue to fall another 1.4% after a 12% plunge on Thursday. Other tech stocks, including Reddit and Amazon also fell, while the Nasdaq index of the largest tech firms listed in the US, ended October with its worst monthly slide since March 2025. While tech firms are spending big on AI, their earnings are not always meeting analysts' expectations, spooking investors and creating fears of an AI bubble. Major tech companies have ramped up artificial intelligence spending, with Meta, Alphabet, Oracle, Amazon, and Microsoft committing to spending $800bn between them in 2026.

items.title: Britain’s blighted high streets will improve by next election, says Rayner
items.summary: Housing secretary says Labour wants to reverse fortunes of towns plagued by boarded-up shops and rogue businesses Angela Rayner has said voters will begin to see a difference in their high street before the next general election as Labour prioritises investment in struggling…
items.body: Angela Rayner has said voters will begin to see a difference in their high street before the next general election as Labour prioritises investment in struggling local communities. The housing secretary said the government had made it a top priority before the country goes to the polls to begin turning around the fortunes of places blighted by boarded-up shops and rogue businesses. “There’s been a real sense of decline,” she said. “People see it as part of the identity of their town and area, and that’s why we’ve got our high streets strategy.” Speaking after John Healey, the chancellor, earmarked more than £1bn in his debut budget on Wednesday to support retail, hospitality and leisure businesses, Rayner signalled that the government stood ready to take further action.

items.title: From strong to stronger: China’s powerhouse provinces propel economy towards GDP target
items.summary: China’s top 10 provincial economies by gross domestic product had a major part in propping up national growth for the first three quarters of 2026, analysts say, putting the regions in a crucial role to help the country meet the economic targets reaffirmed by political leaders…
items.body: China’s top 10 provincial economies by gross domestic product had a major part in propping up national growth for the first three quarters of 2026, analysts say, putting the regions in a crucial role to help the country meet the economic targets reaffirmed by political leaders at the just-concluded fifth plenum. The top 10 provinces were likely to continue their lead for the rest of the year and going into 2027, analysts said, giving Beijing economic confidence and offsetting sluggish performance elsewhere. Nine out of the 10 powerhouse provinces reported growth the same as or higher than the national average of 4.6 per cent between January and September, putting the world’s second-largest economy closer to logging a growth rate within the “4.5 to 5 per cent” benchmark range set for 2026.

items.title: Binance hack: Investigators in a 'cat and mouse game' to recover $6.3 billion in stolen funds
items.summary: More than $6 billion in crypto was stolen from Binance, setting off a race to recover the funds before North Korea-linked hackers can launder them into cash.
items.body: Crypto firms and law enforcement are racing to recover more than $6 billion worth of cryptocurrency stolen from Binance before hackers manage to hide the funds. The firms say they're in a "cat and mouse game" against alleged North Korean hackers who are using a combination of crypto obfuscation techniques and professional global money laundering networks to turn their digital coins into fiat currency, according to experts who spoke to CNBC. These moves underscore how hard it can be to recover the stolen funds after a crypto hack. "Ultimately, they're [hackers] trying to off-ramp it [crypto] to fiat. And that becomes the challenge, that's sort of this race against time," Ari Redbord, global head of policy at TRM Labs, one of the companies investigating the Binance hack, told CNBC on Friday.

items.title: What we know about Binance's $6.3bn hack
items.summary: Cyber correspondent Joe Tidy explains more about what is suspected to be the biggest hack in history.
items.body: Binance, the world's biggest crypto exchange, has been hit by a $6.3bn (£4.7bn) hack - thought to be the biggest in history. Half of the assets have been frozen but many remain in the hands of the hackers, the cryptocurrency giant said. It later added that it has "begun recovering" some funds. Two analytics firms have attributed the incident to a North Korean hacking unit, though no one has claimed responsibility. Binance did not directly respond to questions about the incident's potential links to North Korea. BBC cyber correspondent Joe Tidy explains more about the hack and what to do if you are affected.

items.body: BP’s quarterly profits have been labelled “obscene” after they hit an 18-year high of $8.46bn (£6.3bn), as the war in the Middle East drove up oil and gas prices. The energy company hailed a “banner quarter” on Friday, with its underlying ​replacement ⁠cost profit – a key measure of its income – almost quadrupling in the three months to the end of September, from $2.2bn in the same period ​a year ​ago. The jump meant BP’s quarterly profits hit their highest level since the $8.9bn recorded in 2008 . BP’s chief executive, Meg O’Neill, told Bloomberg TV: “It really was a banner quarter for the refining business. We had very strong margins from the BP-operated refineries, we also had very strong underlying performance.

items.title: Results of the ECB Survey of Professional Forecasters for the fourth quarter of 2026
items.body: Respondents’ expectations for headline inflation, as measured by the Harmonised Index of Consumer Prices (HICP), stood at 3.0% for 2026, 2.6% for 2027 and 2.0% for 2028. Compared with the previous round, these were revised up by 0.3 and 0.4 percentage points for 2026 and 2027 respectively but remained unchanged for 2028. Longer-term expectations (for 2031) remained at 2.0% for both headline and core inflation. A special question, which was also asked in the previous round, concerned the impact of the war in the Middle East. The responses suggested that additional effects of the energy price shock are mainly expected for 2027 but that second-round effects will remain limited. For inflation, the risk balance was tilted to the upside for 2026-28 but remained more balanced thereafter. Respondents expected real GDP growth of 1.0% in 2026 and 1.3% in both 2027 and 2028.

items.title: Chinese firms in Serbia not expecting big changes after change in government
items.summary: Though Serbia’s incoming Student List government called for the resignation of several senior officials and an audit of public projects, some of them built by Chinese contractors, analysts and insiders said it was unlikely the new coalition’s victory would lead to a sea change…
items.body: Though Serbia’s incoming Student List government called for the resignation of several senior officials and an audit of public projects, some of them built by Chinese contractors, analysts and insiders said it was unlikely the new coalition’s victory would lead to a sea change in the business relationship between the two countries. The message at Thursday’s Student List news conference – the first since the electoral coalition defeated former president Aleksandar Vucic’s Serbian Progressive Party (SNS) in Sunday’s parliamentary election – echoed the one sent out months ago in neighbouring Hungary. There, following his triumph over Viktor Orban, Prime Minister Peter Magyar called for senior officials to resign and vowed greater scrutiny of government contracts. Much like Serbia, Chinese firms in Hungary had built up a strong presence following years of strongman rule.

items.title: Binance loses $6.3 billion in crypto heist—what happens to your money when an exchange gets hacked
items.summary: Crypto exchanges make it easier to buy, sell and store digital assets, but they come with risks, too.
items.body: A record-breaking hack at Binance, the world's largest cryptocurrency exchange, is a reminder of the risks investors take when trusting a company to hold their digital tokens. Binance said Friday that the security breach affected about $6.3 billion in client assets , making it the largest crypto hack on record. Around $3 billion of the affected assets has been frozen on blockchain networks, and the exchange says it has begun recovering some of them. Binance's initial investigation suggests hackers gained access to the firm's withdrawal systems and were able to make unauthorized transfers from the exchange's crypto wallets, according to the company . The company says it has found no evidence that the private keys controlling those wallets were leaked and is still investigating the full scope of the breach. The company says it will cover customers' losses .

items.title: City of London chief tops UK Black Powerlist
items.summary: Ian Thomas, who heads the City of London Corporation, tops the Black Powerlist in its 21st year.
items.body: Ian Thomas, chief executive of the City of London Corporation, has been named the UK's most influential Black Briton in this year's Black Powerlist awards. The 57-year old is the first Black person to oversee the Square Mile's governing body in its more than 900-year history. The City of London Corporation is an administrative body with responsibility for London's central financial district, headed by its own Lord Mayor. Thomas tops the 2027 Black Powerlist, which recognises the most powerful people of African and Caribbean heritage in the UK. The award body said he was "a respected public-service leader with over 30 years' experience in local government". Other influential names in this year's top ten include entrepreneurs Emma Grede and Steven Bartlett, as well as actor and filmmaker Sir Idris Elba.

items.title: Poundland in peril: how rampant inflation and price wars left £1 stores exposed
items.summary: With the chain on the brink of administration, its low-profile US owners face questions about their conduct ‘It was a very successful and simple proposition,” laments one former Poundland boss. With every product in the shop sold at £1, and the price in its name, its proposition…
items.body: ‘I t was a very successful and simple proposition,” laments one former Poundland boss. With every product in the shop sold at £1, and the price in its name, its proposition to shoppers was the clearest of any UK high street chain. Now the UK’s first and biggest nationwide single-price retailer could disappear amid heavy competition and inflation that has eaten into its ability to offer bargains. Its potential collapse has brought distress for its up to 12,000 staff in the run-up to Christmas, and as shoppers head to the chain for Halloween costumes and treats. Meanwhile, its low-profile owners are facing questions from the prime minister over their behaviour in the week his government’s budget attempted to offer support to the high street .

items.title: France network outage puts Nokia under scrutiny as EU pushes to phase out Huawei, ZTE gear
items.summary: A mobile network outage in France this week has raised questions about the reliability of Finnish telecoms giant Nokia’s products against the backdrop of continued European Union efforts to phase out Chinese suppliers Huawei Technologies and ZTE over security concerns. The…
items.body: A mobile network outage in France this week has raised questions about the reliability of Finnish telecoms giant Nokia’s products against the backdrop of continued European Union efforts to phase out Chinese suppliers Huawei Technologies and ZTE over security concerns. The problem first hit the network of France’s biggest telecoms provider Orange at 11.37am on Monday and lasted until 8.30pm, resulting in outages of up to nine hours for some customers, Orange France CEO Jerome Henique told French newspaper Le Figaro. At the core of the outage was a software bug in Nokia’s code, Henique said, adding that the flaw was new to Orange and “extremely complicated to find”. The bug affected Orange’s mobile core network as well as equipment designed to provide redundancy for the core network, making the situation exceptional, according to him.

items.title: The big questions remaining after Anthropic’s blockbuster IPO prospectus
items.summary: Uncertainties remain ahead of one of the most hotly anticipated IPOs in history.
items.body: This report is from this week's The Tech Download newsletter. Like what you see? You can subscribe here. Anthropic's over 300 page S-1 filing earlier this week contained a lot of information. It was the most comprehensive public statement to date about how a pure-play AI lab makes its money. After the prospectus went live on Monday, my U.S.-based colleagues and I went through it with a fine-tooth comb , detailing everything from revenue and risks to competitors and computing costs. The filing also revealed that CEO Dario Amodei and his six co-founders each own over 200 million shares, which could be worth billions if Anthropic hits the over $1 trillion valuation it's expected to. Anthropic reported its cost of revenue as $2.38 billion in the first half of 2026, booking $16.29 billion in revenue during the same period and implying a gross margin of 85%.

items.title: How Poundland grew from a market stall to a high street giant
items.summary: The retail giant - which started life at a Wolverhampton market - is now at threat of collapse.
items.body: That is how Steve Smith, the founder of Poundland, describes the genesis of the budget giant - which went on to employ thousands of people and see over a million customers a week - on his own website , external . But now the West Midlands-based retailer is teetering on the edge , after its US-based owners Gordon Brothers cut off a vital funding supply and rejected a takeover offer from Irish firm Martin Property Group. Having spent time on his parents stall since the age of two Wolverhampton-born businessman Smith started out in the very same place - selling items for £1 from his own stall. After a £50,000 loan from his parents he opened the first Poundland shop , in The Octagon Shopping Centre in Burton-upon-Trent, Staffordshire, on 13 December 1990. That first day, with a range of 624 products, the store took more than £13,000 - "and Poundland was born," Smith said.

items.title: ‘You can see the water going down’: residents on edge as one of England’s worst-hit reservoirs dries up
items.summary: After UK’s hottest summer on record, Ardingly near Haywards Heath is just 19% full – and next-closest reservoir is unusable due to broken treatment works “You can see the water level at Ardingly going down and down. I don’t remember ever seeing it this low,” says Caroline Allan,…
items.body: “Y ou can see the water level at Ardingly going down and down. I don’t remember ever seeing it this low,” says Caroline Allan, a lifetime resident of Haywards Heath, the nearest town to one of England’s most depleted reservoirs. The Ardingly reservoir, managed by South East Water and serving about 95,000 properties in and around Haywards Heath and Uckfield in Sussex, is currently 19% full. The day the Guardian visited, the weather was grey and rainy, incongruous with the muddy reservoir bed that should have been submerged under six metres of water. Earlier this month a severe drought was declared in parts of Devon, Cornwall, Dorset, Somerset, East Sussex and West Sussex, with urgent measures being taken to secure public water supplies after the UK experienced its hottest summer on record .

items.title: Pinglu Canal off to ‘encouraging start’ in China’s push to boost trade with Southeast Asia
items.summary: China’s newly opened Pinglu Canal handled more than 1 million tonnes (1.1 million short tons) of cargo in its first month of operation, giving the country’s southwestern hinterland more direct access to international markets, particularly in Southeast Asia. The milestone was…
items.body: China’s newly opened Pinglu Canal handled more than 1 million tonnes (1.1 million short tons) of cargo in its first month of operation, giving the country’s southwestern hinterland more direct access to international markets, particularly in Southeast Asia. The milestone was reached on October 17, when a laden cargo vessel passed through a key lock on the canal in southern China’s Guangxi Zhuang autonomous region, heading towards Qinzhou Port on the Gulf of Tonkin, known in China as the Beibu Gulf, Guangxi Daily reported recently. The 134.2km (83.4-mile) waterway opened to navigation on September 16, allowing cargo from inland provinces to reach the sea without taking a roughly 560km detour via Guangzhou, the capital of neighbouring Guangdong province.

items.title: 'Bad time to troll': Binance co-founder Zhao asks Musk for support after hack
items.summary: Binance co-founder Changpeng Zhao asked Elon Musk to stop “trolling” after a $6.3 billion hack, pointing to Binance’s $1 billion-plus SpaceX stake.
items.body: Changpeng Zhao, the cofounder and former CEO of Binance , asked Elon Musk not to "troll" the company on Friday and instead "show some support" after the SpaceX CEO appeared to mock the embattled cryptocurrency exchange in a series of social media posts. After learning the world's largest crypto exchange had been hit by a $6.3 billion hack late Thursday, Musk posted several emojis, ranging from laughing to grimacing, on X. In response, Zhao reminded the SpaceX and Tesla CEO of Binance's equity stake in Musk's businesses. Binance’s SpaceX stake, which stems from an earlier investment in what was then-Twitter, is worth more than $1 billion, Zhao said. "Elon, have a lot of respect for you, but bad time to troll. Please stop," Zhao wrote. "Our SPCX shares (from our $500m investment in your Twitter takeover) are worth more than a billion. Would appreciate if you show a little support.

items.title: How video game remakes tap the power of nostalgia
items.summary: Video games are good at triggering nostalgia, a key reason why classic games keep getting remade.
items.body: The moment she saw footage from the remake of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time, Kacey Doran picked up her phone. She had to tell her sister. Nearly 30 years ago, a 10-year-old Doran had sat in front of her family's TV, reading out the dialogue on screen to her sister, a year younger, as they inched their way through the original Nintendo 64 game's sprawling, puzzle-filled dungeons. Ocarina's fantasy-like story, and beautiful music, enthralled them both. It was also the first game Doran ever completed. Now, countless memories rushed back to her as she devoured clips of the fully redesigned version, due to arrive on the Switch 2 later this year. This is the power of nostalgia – and a perfect example of how video games can trigger it. Doran now teaches an esports course at Rowan University in New Jersey.

items.title: Andy Burnham admits he would have liked more radical first budget
items.summary: Prime minister says room for manoeuvre was limited by geopolitical crises and Labour’s 2024 manifesto Andy Burnham has admitted his first budget as prime minister was not as radical as he would have liked because of the economic uncertainty facing the country. He said he would…
items.body: Andy Burnham has admitted his first budget as prime minister was not as radical as he would have liked because of the economic uncertainty facing the country. He said he would have liked to have gone further with this week’s announcement – including with higher energy support payments – but felt hemmed in by external events such as the war in Iran, which has pushed up borrowing costs. Burnham’s chancellor, John Healey , announced a range of relatively inexpensive measures on Wednesday, including a £100 payment for most households to help with energy bills this winter. He has faced criticism for not doing enough on a range of issues including defence spending, welfare cuts and support for the cost of living. Burnham told ITV: “The room for manoeuvre wasn’t what I would have hoped it to be. I guess then the question is, you know, radical within what we were able to do.

items.title: Reddit stock plunges 29% after weak outlook, wrapping its worst day ever
items.summary: Reddit shares sank on Friday after the company issued weak Q4 sales guidance and announced it will test requiring users to log in to see content.
items.body: Shares of Reddit cratered 29.22% on Friday, the worst drop since becoming a public company in 2024, after the company forecast weak fourth-quarter sales in its latest earnings report . The social media company on Thursday projected fourth-quarter sales between $1 billion and $1.03 billion, below analysts' estimates of $1.05 billion. Reddit reported Q3 sales growth of 53% over a year ago, weaker than previous quarters, but beat Wall Street expectations on both earnings and revenue. The report comes as the company has seen a shift in its search referral traffic with the rise of Google's AI Overview. In an interview with CNBC, Reddit CEO Steve Huffman said search-referral traffic from Google went "down meaningfully in this quarter" due to AI.

items.title: From Levi's to Primark - the fashion chains selling mended clothes
items.summary: A new generation is embracing eye-catching patching and visible mends.
items.body: If Alice Brown is browsing in second-hand shops and finds a jumper with a hole, that won't stop her buying it. Over the last year she has developed her own unique style, needle-felting cute animals and insects to cover moth holes, stains and other imperfections, winning her a huge following online. "The natural place for decoration is in the centre at the front. If the hole is under the arm or on the shoulder, it forces you to think about the design," she says. Often dubbed "visible mending" the trend is spreading from hobby crafters and community workshops, even drawing in fast-fashion brands and reaching the designer catwalks this year. At one Saturday morning workshop in Brighton, Jayne Eagle shows her students how to attach a patch of fabric behind a tear so the cat-face design peeps through.

items.title: UK house prices grow at slowest pace in two years as mortgage rates rise
items.summary: Average price for property stands at £273,566 in October, flat on previous month, says Nationwide Business live – latest updates UK house prices grew by an annual rate of just 0.5% in October, the slowest pace in more than two years, as higher mortgage rates put off potential…
items.body: UK house prices grew by an annual rate of just 0.5% in October, the slowest pace in more than two years, as higher mortgage rates put off potential buyers. The average price for a property in the UK stood at £273,566 in October, flat on the previous month and down from 0.8% in the year to September, according to the lender Nationwide . The slowdown in the market comes as buyers face higher borrowing costs. This month the average cost of a five-year fixed-rate mortgage hit the 6% barrier for the first time in three years . The average stood at 5.99% on Thursday, according to the financial information provider Moneyfacts, while the average two-year rate was not far behind at 5.97%. There has been no change in the Bank of England base rate since last December but volatility in the bond market has driven up the swap rates that influence the pricing of fixed-rate mortgages.

items.body: Yorkshire Water's chief executive has announced she is to step down, just 24 hours after the company was given the lowest possible environmental rating by the Environment Agency. Nicola Shaw, who has led the firm since 2022, will leave the role on 1 January to be replaced by Nicola Medalova, a chartered environmental health officer who previously worked for the National Grid. In a statement on Friday, Shaw said it had been a "privilege" to lead the company but that it was the "right time" to leave her post. Shaw has faced criticism in recent years, including for taking £1.9m in undisclosed payments between 2023 and 2026, while the company has come under scrutiny for its performance. items.title: Streeting denies 'kicking can down the road' in defence spending row
items.summary: The government is under pressure to set out a path to greater defence spending, as ministers unveil plans to boost UK firms.
items.body: Defence Secretary Wes Streeting has denied "kicking the can down the road" over how much the UK spends on defence. The government has faced criticism for not setting out a pathway at Wednesday's Budget to hit its target of spending 3% of GDP on defence by 2030. It comes as Chancellor John Healey and Streeting announce that foreign firms which are awarded defence contracts of more than £50m will need to invest an equal value back into the UK. Under the new investment rules, described as an "offset strategy", these companies will need to spend an equivalent amount on British factories, jobs and training. The Ministry of Defence will apply the rules on a "case-by-case" basis from April 2027, the government said. Healey and Streeting will unveil the policy on a visit to UK defence contractor BAE's shipbuilding site in Glasgow later.

items.body: The amount Britons can earn from a side hustle without paying tax will rise to £3,000 next year in a fillip for those who make extra cash from hobbies or reselling. Up to 1.4 million people could benefit from the change announced in the budget , with the chancellor confirming the tax-free “trading” allowance will increase from £1,000 to £3,000 in April 2027. The number of Britons with a side hustle has exploded in recent years, with reselling clothes, tutoring and dog-walking among the popular avenues to create extra income at a time when household finances are under pressure. Last year, 2.6 million people made money selling goods through platforms including eBay , Vinted and Etsy, according to data provided by HM Revenue and Customs (HMRC) to accountancy firm Lubbock Fine. In 2024 the number was just 450,000.

items.title: Binance's $6.3 billion hack: What we know and what comes next
items.summary: Billions in crypto assets have been frozen following a potential Binance security breach, raising questions about whether the funds can be recovered.
items.body: Binance was hacked with an estimated impact of $6.3 billion, raising questions about the recovery of stolen funds and the broader fallout for crypto markets. Around $3 billion in cryptocurrency assets have been frozen so far, according to a Binance security update . The exchange pledged to cover all losses, while blockchain investigators linked the attack to North Korea and analysts assessed the potential financial risks. Freezing cryptocurrency prevents it from being transferred, but recovering the funds requires a separate legal process, according to Ari Redbord, global head of policy at blockchain intelligence firm TRM Labs and a former U.S. federal prosecutor and Treasury official. "A freeze stops the money from moving, and recovery follows through legal process," Redbord told CNBC.

items.body: The world’s largest cryptocurrency exchange has been hit by a $6.3bn heist that, according to experts, is likely to be the work of North Korea . It could be the biggest heist of any kind in history, according to Elliptic, a consultancy specialising in crypto-related crime. The incident, which took place late on Thursday, is more than four times bigger than the previous largest crypto hack, the $1.5bn one targeting the Bybit exchange last year . Elliptic says there does not appear to be anything comparable in the pre-crypto era. “This incident is almost certainly the single largest known theft of any kind,” says Tom Robinson, the consultancy’s chief scientist. “Before Bybit, that record was held by Saddam Hussein, who took $1bn from the central bank of Iraq in Baghdad on the eve of the 2003 Iraq war.

items.title: How elections worldwide are testing Trump’s influence abroad
items.summary: Recent election losses by leaders linked to Trump have prompted questions about whether his influence over the global right is weakening.
items.body: In August , President Donald Trump claimed that 97% of Republican candidates he backed had won their primary races. And it's true that Trump has shown an ability to influence races particularly in Republican primaries, picking off politicians he didn't like such as Sen. John Cornyn, R-Texas, and Rep. Thomas Massie, R-Ky. But while he hasn't shied away from expressing his opinions on foreign leaders, his influence over other countries' elections is proving less strong. Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva won reelection on Sunday, defeating Trump-aligned Flávio Bolsonaro, whose father Jair had also been a Trump ally. Also last weekend, a student-led movement in Serbia defeated the ruling party of Aleksandar Vucic, a populist leader who had cultivated ties with Trump and his circle. Vucic had served as Serbia's president from 2017, and as prime minister from 2014 to 2017.

items.title: Crypto giant Binance hit by $6.3bn hack suspected to be largest in history
items.summary: Two analytics firms have attributed the incident to a North Korean hacking unit called TraderTraitor.
items.body: Cryptocurrency giant Binance said on Thursday that $6.3bn (£4.7bn) of digital assets have been impacted by what is thought to be the biggest crypto hack on record. The world's biggest crypto exchange said about half of those assets had been frozen but that many remained in the hands of the hackers, adding that it will "cover all losses". The company said while initial checks suggested an engineer's laptop had been compromised, allowing an attacker to make unauthorised withdrawals, "our subsequent investigation has uncovered additional points of breach". Two analytics firms have attributed the incident, which eclipses a record-setting $1.5bn hack on the Bybit exchange in 2025, to a North Korean hacking unit called TraderTraitor. Cyber-security firm Check Point said the unit is also known in the industry as Lazarus Group, which has been blamed for the 2025 hack.

items.title: Opening the EU debate again is clearly a political minefield. But we have to do it | Simon Jenkins
items.summary: Andy Burnham must tread cautiously, but Brexit was a very grave act of self-harm – and he is right to address it Andy Burnham’s opening debate on whether Britain should rejoin the EU is divisive, painful and politically risky. That is why it should be welcomed. To jeopardise his…
items.body: A ndy Burnham’s opening debate on whether Britain should rejoin the EU is divisive, painful and politically risky. That is why it should be welcomed. To jeopardise his popularity so soon after coming to office might seem reckless, but the issue is urgent and not going away. Brexit is continuing to damage the nation’s economy. The prime minister’s job is to challenge, if not reform it. The Brexit decade has evoked a bizarre sense of guilt among Britons. Opinion polls show nearly 60% regard it as a mistake, with just a third still in favour. Almost a quarter of those who voted for Brexit now regret it. While early forecasts of economic disaster were proved wrong , the accumulated cost of cutting links with Britain’s biggest trading partner is estimated at 6-8% of GDP . This is huge. It must rank as the greatest act of self-harm by a British government in modern times.

Emergency power cuts came into force in Dnipro and Dnipropetrovsk Oblast early Friday after damage from Russian attacks, according to Ukrainian private energy company DTEK. More than 350,000 people were left without power and work is ongoing to restore supply, Oleksandr Hanzha, the head of the military administration in the region, said in a Telegram post. An oil refinery in the Russian city of Novokuibyshevsk in Samara Oblast that produced jet fuel for the Russian armed forces was set on fire after being hit by a Ukrainian drone.

items.summary: ‘Even though economists warned that tariffs would be inflationary, Trump has enthusiastically embraced them’ Donald Trump successfully campaigned for his second term two years ago promising to reduce prices on day one , but ever since he returned to the White House, he has done…
items.body: Donald Trump successfully campaigned for his second term two years ago promising to reduce prices on day one , but ever since he returned to the White House, he has done little to fight inflation or reduce prices. Instead, some of his most important policy decisions – most notably his war against Iran and his tariff wars – have increased inflation instead of reducing it. This helps explain why more than one in five Americans who voted for Trump now disapprove of the job he’s doing. Even though economists warned that tariffs would be inflationary, Trump has enthusiastically embraced them during his second term. Indeed, the “ liberation day ” tariffs he imposed soon after returning to office increased the price of hundreds of goods, including citrus fruits , steel, bananas, beef and auto parts.

items.body: Halloween shoppers in the US seeking sweet relief this spooky season have instead been shocked by the high price of seasonal treats, as cost of living pressures continue to bite. Demetrio Beltres, a 33-year-old financial adviser searching for Halloween bargains for trick or treaters said he was spending more than his usual $15 (£11) to $20 this year because prices were much higher. "I'm trying to spend at least $20 to $30 just to make sure that I get the kids something," he said, while browsing the rows of colour options at a Target in Manhattan. Stephen Zagor, adjunct associate professor at Columbia Business School, said people have only so much to spend, and when everyday essentials are costing more, people may feel less inclined to make this the most extravagant Halloween.

items.title: The Iran war is deepening the US energy crisis. A bad winter is ahead | Mark Wolfe
items.summary: Congress must act to ensure that families are able to heat their homes before the start of the season Heating oil may be the clearest warning yet of how the war in Iran is deepening the US’s energy affordability crisis. Families who heat their homes with oil are facing bills…
items.body: H eating oil may be the clearest warning yet of how the war in Iran is deepening the US’s energy affordability crisis. Families who heat their homes with oil are facing bills that could be 50% higher this winter, adding nearly $900 to the cost of keeping their homes warm. These families were already struggling before the war began. As the Guardian recently reported , research by my organization found that electricity shutoffs in 10 states had increased 28% over the past two years. Millions of Americans were already falling behind on their utility bills, forced to choose between paying for energy, food, medicine and rent. Now they face another round of increases in gasoline, electricity and home heating costs. The war didn’t create America’s energy affordability crisis. But it is making a bad situation much worse.

items.body: The Be Ready campaign may offer sensible advice in principle ( Every Briton should stockpile water and food supplies, government advises, 22 October ), but as a midwife working in Tower Hamlets, one of the poorest boroughs in London, I can see first-hand that its practical recommendations risk excluding precisely those families who are already most vulnerable. Chevron shares are up nearly 2% while Exxon is more than 1% higher. Both touched all-time highs Friday. The world is facing a fuel crisis as Ukraine, Iran and Houthi militants attack refineries in Russia and the Middle East, reducing global capacity by millions of barrels per day. Importers have increasingly turned to U.S. Gulf Coast refineries for diesel supplies as a consequence. ExxonMobil's profits doubled to $15.4 billion, or $3.72 a share, compared to $7.5 billion, or $1.76 a share, in the same period in 2025. items.title: Mercury, lead and methanol found in counterfeit beauty products seized across UK
items.summary: Copies of popular cosmetics and skincare products more likely to contain toxic substances, Trading Standards warns Mercury, lead and methanol have been found in counterfeit beauty products seized across the UK, Trading Standards has said. There is a rising problem with fake…
items.body: Mercury, lead and methanol have been found in counterfeit beauty products seized across the UK, Trading Standards has said. There is a rising problem with fake beauty products, with scammers selling copies of popular and expensive brands. Cosmetics, skincare and perfumes are now among the watchdog’s most commonly investigated fakes. Tests found 13,200 parts per million of mercury in one skincare product, high levels of lead in lipstick, eyeshadow and contour products, nicotine in perfume and a counterfeit fragrance made up of about 80% methanol , a toxic alcohol that can cause serious poisoning. About 20% of 18- to 24-year-olds who bought beauty products last year knowingly bought counterfeits, up from 6% in 2023, according to the latest Intellectual Property Office (IPO) counterfeit goods tracker.

Days before, Barclays cut its forecast for the drug's peak sales after detailed results from two late-stage trials showed the drug had reduced relapses in MS patients by less than analysts expected. It highlights a challenge for Novartis as it prepares to outline its long-term growth strategy in mid-November. The drugmaker reported sales growth this week despite losing key patent protection for blockbuster heart drug Entresto. But Barclays analysts said that the market is already looking to the next patent cliff, with bestsellers Kisqali and Kesimpta facing patent expirations around 2032.

items.title: UN retains Bangladesh and Nepal's least developed country status
items.body: DHAKA -- Bangladesh and Nepal, two struggling South Asian economies, have been granted three more years before graduating from least developed country (LDC) status, easing their trade access as they make further preparations for reclassification after successive internal and external shocks.

items.title: California high-speed rail chief quits amid billowing expenses scandal
items.summary: Ian Choudri resigns after report found agency overseeing troubled LA-San Francisco project misused over $600,000 in public funds The chief executive of California’s embattled high-speed rail authority abruptly resigned on Wednesday, over a month after a state watchdog determined…
items.body: The chief executive of California’s embattled high-speed rail authority abruptly resigned on Wednesday, over a month after a state watchdog determined the agency had misused public funds. In September, California’s office of the inspector general released an investigative report finding that the rail authority had paid $543,000 in travel-related reimbursements for consultants that were not allowed, including international or out-of-state travel expenses. The report raised questions about whether business and pleasure was mixed under the purview of the chief executive, Ian Choudri. The rail authority paid $81,000 for consultants’ travel expenses to places that lacked an official purpose, including gyms, an escape room and a nightclub. In his resignation email, which CalMatters obtained , Choudri cited “important personal and family priorities”.

items.title: BP’s third-quarter profit nearly quadruples to $8.5 billion as refining margins surge
items.summary: The oil major was the latest to smash profit expectations as global conflicts continue to drive energy market volatility.
items.body: Oil major BP smashed third-quarter expectations on Friday, as volatile energy markets and high refining margins saw profits nearly quadruple year-on-year. The company reported $8.5 billion in underlying replacement cost profit, used as a proxy for net profit. That was above the $6.191 billion forecast by analysts in an LSEG-compiled consensus and up from $2.2 billion a year ago . Operating cash flow hit $28.55 billion across the first nine months of the year, up from $16.89 billion in 2025, while net debt fell to $13.87 billion from $26.05 billion across the same period. The result primarily reflects better performance in gas and marketing trading, and "significantly higher" realized refining margins, BP said. "These are dynamic times with volatility and disruption to trade flows continuing to define energy markets," BP CEO Meg O'Neill said in a statement.

items.title: BOJ chief Ueda says 2% inflation goal not yet sustainably achieved
items.body: TOKYO -- Bank of Japan Gov. Kazuo Ueda on Friday emphasized that while underlying inflation is broadly consistent with 2%, the central bank does not believe its price stability goal has yet been achieved sustainably and stably.

items.title: Watch: Hundreds queue for city's new Lego store
items.summary: Fans queued for hours ahead of the opening of a new Lego Store in Norwich.
items.body: Hundreds of people queued for the opening of a new Lego store in Norfolk on Thursday morning. The shop opened its doors at Chantry Place shopping centre on St Stephen's Street in Norwich at 09:00 GMT. The first person in the queue had been there since 04:00 GMT. Al, 23, joined the queue at 05:00 GMT and told BBC Radio Norfolk: "We've wanted one here for so long. It's going to pull people from such a large area. I can't believe we haven't had it sooner." Before the Norwich store opened, the nearest official Lego Store for many Norfolk shoppers was in Stratford, east London. items.title: Billionaire tax: how a union leader’s ‘crazy’ idea became the defining issue of California’s midterms
items.summary: It was an ambitious notion – now Californians will vote on a one-time 5% billionaire tax, and state’s super rich have pulled out all the stops in opposition One year ago, the idea of a billionaire tax in California was still in its infancy. It wasn’t yet one of the most…
items.body: One year ago, the idea of a billionaire tax in California was still in its infancy. It wasn’t yet one of the most contentious ballot measure fights in state history – pitting Democrats against Democrats, drawing national attention from political heavyweights, and netting hundreds of millions of Silicon Valley dollars to fight it. Back then, it was a bold and desperate answer to Donald Trump’s healthcare cuts. Trump had just signed the One Big Beautiful Bill Act, which dictated a trillion dollars of Medicaid, Affordable Care Act and other healthcare funding be cut over the next decade to offset sweeping tax cuts. When the bill goes into effect in January, that could mean more than 3.4m Californians will lose their coverage, including millions of children.

items.title: Indian AI infrastructure firm reportedly seeks to raise $3 billion of debt to buy Nvidia's next-generation chips
items.summary: Within two years, AM Intelligence plans to set up 400 MW of compute capacity using Nvidia's Rubin graphics processing units.
items.body: An artificial intelligence infrastructure firm in India is reportedly seeking to raise debt to fund the purchase of Nvidia's Rubin graphics processing units. AM Intelligence, a Hyderabad-based company, is planning to raise up to $3 billion through bond issues and bank loans to purchase Nvidia Corp's next-generation chips, Bloomberg reported on Friday . The split between bonds and loans is yet to be finalized, but the firm expects to get $300 million in advance payment from potential offtakers, the report said. AM Intelligence, which claims to be among the "largest committed buyers" of Rubin GPUs outside of North America, did not respond to CNBC's request for comment.

items.title: Foxconn chief downplays AI bubble concerns, sees strong 2027 growth
items.body: TAIPEI -- Foxconn's chairman on Friday downplayed concerns about a possible artificial intelligence bubble, saying demand for the key Nvidia server supplier was clear and strong, and sales growth was expected to be double-digit in 2027.
